answer: Require every agent to lock a slashable stake before it can trade, and tie that stake to a slow-growing reputation built from completed work. A sybil farm must fund each fake identity and wait weeks for its reputation to mature, so mass-producing identities costs real capital and time. Like timber that only gains value after years of growth, a nebula of fresh accounts stays dim until proven: new identities start in a sable-dark trust zone with strict rate limits and tiny transaction caps, so even a thousand clones cannot move meaningful volume before honest peers flag them.
